survey: A stone park chess table with two round stone stools on grass. The table is a thick square slab with rounded edges and a dark-blue and cream checkerboard set into the top. The board faces up and is seen at three-quarter view from above. Under the slab, a square collar sits on a flared, waisted pedestal, which stands on a wider stepped square plinth resting flat on the grass, with a contact shadow. Each stool is a single turned stone piece: a round seat, a waisted octagonal-ish body and a round foot, standing on the grass. One stool is front-left and one is right of the table, at sitting distance and facing the board. The table is a monolithic block, so there are no hinges, cables or loose parts. The pedestal sits centered under the slab, so the load path holds. The board is square and inset evenly inside the rim, with an ordinary checker pattern.

errors.where: Tabletop slab, front-left rim, about a quarter of the way in from the left corner
errors.what: A single vertical seam splits the rim from the top surface down through the edge. It makes the slab look like two blocks butted together, but nothing matches it on the other sides, and the stone on both sides of it carries on as one piece. It reads as a stray split line, not a real joint.

fix: Make the stone tabletop one continuous slab with no vertical seam or split line on its front-left rim. The rounded edge should run smoothly all the way around the checkerboard.
